title: Widen the settled-rule regexes for timestamp writers and directory listing (O-031)
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: FAIL W01 fires the timestamp rule, 0 hit(s): File.SetAttributes(path, FileAttributes.Normal); ... FAIL L02 fires the listing rule, 0 hit(s): var subs = dir.GetDirectories(); — 7 check(s) failed.

Rule 2 ('only the directory-listing open path may write a file-system timestamp', .taad/fitness.yaml:746-764) matches File.SetAttributes in src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.cs outside its excepted files: missing
Rule 4 ('only DirectoryReader lists a directory', .taad/fitness.yaml:774-791) matches the DirectoryInfo instance listings GetFiles(...) and GetDirectories(...): missing
A second, unfenced timestamp/attribute writer or directory listing in Core outside the one sanctioned call site fails a settled rule (no settled rule stays green on it): missing

Scope: spike 1's union (rule 2 at 11 patterns, rule 4 at 7, a new entry, 21 plant rows) against the R2-m4 two-line minimum, which alone closes the repro (spike 2). The practice designer raised over_engineering_flag against their own union. The trimmed version keeps `\bFile\.SetAttributes\b`, GetFiles|GetDirectories in the instance pattern, the because-text fix and rows S58, S64 and S65, and drops everything else.

Placement of the new entry: the engine appends it at the end of the file under '# settled by SL-104' (this design), or it is hand-inserted after rule 4 so the three sibling fences read together (the proposal). Only the first marker matters to any tool.

The Attributes setter in a separate entry that excepts DirectoryReader.cs, against a narrower right-hand-side pattern (one that requires FileAttributes) inside rule 2. The narrower pattern misses `fi.Attributes = attrs;`.
Rewriting the because-texts to list what is fenced and what escapes, against simply deleting the 'every way' sentence.
